caption: Pulmonary valve, normal and pulmonary hypertension (columns): RV pressure (black, upstream), pulmonary-trunk pressure PT (grey, downstream), the transvalvar pressure difference dp (panel shown from -3 to 7 mmHg) and A_eff. Each column digitised every 0.005 s into mynard2012_fig6_pulmonary_<case>_pressures.csv (P_up = RV, P_down = PT, dp = RV - PT from the digitised pressures; u in Pa) and mynard2012_fig6_pulmonary_<case>_A_eff.csv. Time from the 0.2 s scale bar (900.0 px/s); t = 0 at each column's left edge (left axis, column separator); the columns are 0.978 and 0.961 s wide, more than the 0.89 s beat: the RV upstroke at t = 0.09 s recurs at the right edge. Pressure axes from the ticks 0-60 mmHg, dp from -2 to 6, A_eff from 2-6 cm2 (0 from the tick spacing). Where the grey PT line is hidden under RV, PT = RV - dp(panel). normal: RV 1.5-20.7 mmHg, PT 10.1-18.6 mmHg, RV rises above PT at 0.120 s and falls below at 0.340 s, peak dp 2.59 mmHg at 0.196 s, A_eff max 7.08 cm2 (Table III: M_st 1 x A_ann 7.1), A_eff > 0.05 cm2 from 0.120 to 0.510 s; pulmonary hypertension: RV 3.0-69.2 mmHg, PT 34.8-69.4 mmHg, RV above PT from 0.140 to 0.240 s and again from 0.260 to 0.445 s (mid-systolic reversal, dp min -2.19 mmHg at 0.245 s), peak dp 5.74 mmHg at 0.141 s at the image resolution (the 0.005 s samples reach 4.78: the spike is about 0.01 s wide), A_eff max 7.06 cm2, notch d down to 3.95 cm2 at 0.255 s, A_eff > 0.05 cm2 from 0.140 to 0.510 s.
